transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes

Attendees:
- Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE)
- Priya Patel (Redwood SE)
- Evan Liu (Redwood CSM)
- Carlos Vega (Lumenix CTO)
- Mei Chen (Lumenix Senior ML Eng)
- Asha Kapoor (Lumenix Platform Lead)
- Ravi Desai (Lumenix PM)

Summary:
Quick scoping to align on success criteria for the POC, map out milestone dates (kickoff, access & infra, mid-point benchmark review, exec readout), and agree on workload size and benchmark metrics. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, VPC/KMS constraints, and required artifacts. Agreed to a 6-week sprint with mid-point check and final exec readout.

Topics:
- POC success criteria (latency/quality/cost targets)
- Access gating (SSO, VPC, KMS) and timeline
- Workload sizing and sampling strategy
- Benchmark metrics & pass/fail gates
- Staffing and sprint milestones

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: alright everyone can hear me? cool thanks for hopping on. we're gonna run through the POC plan, make sure we have the gates and who owns what.
[00:22] Carlos: yep hearing you. thanks for putting this together — we want to make sure we can present something solid to executives in early Jan.
[00:35] Jordan: perfect, thank you. real quick introductions then I want to confirm scope. Priya, you'll drive the benchmarks with me; Evan will be the CSM for access cadence.
[00:46] Priya: hi all, Priya from Redwood SE. i'll own the benchmark config, runner, and help interpret perf/quality tradeoffs.
[00:55] Mei: Mei here — we'll provide sample traffic and the priority prompts. we have some complex multi-turn flows and a few high-cardinality inputs.
[01:05] Asha: Asha — platform; i'll handle networking and infra approvals. we'll need to know if this is hosted or dedicated early because of procurement.
[01:18] Jordan: good point. quick ask: what's your current peak qps and p95 latency targets? just ballpark numbers.
[01:28] Ravi: We're aiming for 10 qps steady across peak windows, p95 around 300-350 ms ideally, but we can tolerate up to 500 if cost is significantly lower.
[01:39] Priya: ok that's useful. for the POC we'll run two benchmark profiles: a latency-focused run (single-stream, low concurrency) and a throughput run (batching behavior, ten concurrent workers). we'll measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1k tokens.
[01:58] Mei: are you assuming the Redwood hosted API? or are we evaluating a dedicated pool? our data governance team prefers VPC/private but we can run hosted for initial perf checks if that's easier?
[02:12] Jordan: we recommend starting hosted to validate model choice and prompt tuning — lower friction — then shift to dedicated or private deployment for the exec readout if you need isolation. note: hosted may show slightly better latency because of multitenant warm caches, but dedicated gives predictability under sustained load.
[02:34] Carlos: procurement will push for dedicated for SLA reasons. can we quantify the delta and produce a cost model?
[02:41] Priya: yes we'll capture both. our benchmark spreadsheet will include cost estimates for hosted (per-token) and dedicated (reserved GPU hours + amortized tokens). I'll attach that.
[02:55] Jordan: let's walk through the timeline — propose six weeks: Week 0 kick: access + onboarding; Week 1 prompt tuning and small-scale runs; Week 3 mid-point benchmark review; Week 4-5 optimizations and dedicated tests; Week 6 exec readout. Thoughts?
[03:12] Mei: that seems tight but doable if we get access quickly. bandwidth is the main unknown.
[03:20] Asha: yes network window for VPC peering currently open next Tuesday or the following Friday. we need a clear list of ports and peer IPs.
[03:29] Jordan: we'll provide a short access checklist: SSO/SAML metadata, VPC peering CIDR, KMS requirements, sample traces, and a service account. Evan will own the checklist delivery.
[03:41] Evan: noted, i'll send the checklist with timing options.
[03:46] Ravi: also governance — audit logs and retention. we need SOC 2 scope and whether logs can be pushed to our SIEM.
[03:55] Priya: Redwood has audit logs available for Dedicated and Private; hosted offers basic logs but for SIEM forwarding we'd use Dedicated or Private. we'll note exact retention windows in the security pack.
[04:10] Carlos: okay good. what are the success criteria you typically use?
[04:14] Jordan: typically customer-defined but a recommended matrix: functional quality (semantic correctness on a 50 prompt test set, >90% pass rate), latency (p95 <= 500ms for latency profile), throughput (sustained 8-12 qps with p95 within SLO), and cost (expected cost per 1M tokens within customer's budget). Also operational criteria: ability to decrypt in customer KMS and VPC peering validated.
[04:40] Mei: 50 prompt test set — can we augment with our production prompts? we have some golden examples.
[04:46] Priya: absolutely — bring your golden prompts; we'll run them as part of the quality gate. we'll also do a few adversarial inputs.
[04:55] Carlos: you mentioned KV cache optimizations earlier in the doc, can that help reduce p95?
[05:01] Priya: yes, prefix KV caching and session pinning can bring down repeated-token costs and reduce latency for multi-turn. we'll simulate typical conversation lengths in the runner. note: some of our kernel-level optimizations (we call them compilation/kern select) vary by quantization and sequence length. sometimes transcription shows that as "kern- selection" which was confusing last time.
[05:26] Jordan: we should also talk about quant profiles. do you need full FP16 or are you okay with 4-bit quant?
[05:33] Mei: legal/infra prefers standards but will accept quant if it doesn't degrade quality beyond 2% on our metrics.
[05:41] Priya: we'll include a quant step: baseline FP16, q4_0 and q4_1 runs, measure quality delta per prompt set.
[05:50] Asha: how invasive is the private deployment? our security team is cautious about IAM service accounts and firewall rules.
[05:57] Jordan: private requires more setup: VPC peering, KMS integration (customer-managed key optional), and a small agent install for on-prem but we can provide a checklist. It's usually 2-5 business days to get peering + keys approved depending on security reviews.
[06:13] Ravi: let's map owners: Jordan — overall POC, Priya — benchmarks, Evan — access & ops sync, Mei — sample data & prompt set, Asha — infra approvals.
[06:23] Jordan: yes that matches what we had in the chat. I'll draft a milestone calendar and zap it over.
[06:30] 
[06:45] Jordan: diving into benchmark specifics: we'll run three experiments — 1) latency single-stream (p95 target), 2) concurrency scaling to 10-20 qps to test batching, 3) long multi-turn sessions to validate KV cache behavior. How many unique sessions do you want to simulate?
[07:02] Mei: our modal traffic is ~40k unique sessions/day; for POC maybe simulate 5k sessions over a 2 hour window to reproduce warm-cache behavior.
[07:13] Priya: ok 5k sessions in the runner is doable; we'll also do warm/cold cache toggles. We'll capture tokens per request distribution.
[07:22] Carlos: on metrics, make sure to export raw traces — tokenization mismatches sometimes throw off cost calc, last time the tokenizer split unknown symbols weirdly.
[07:33] Priya: good call; we'll store both token counts and raw request/response for spot checks.
[07:39] Evan: for the mid-point review — suggest a 60 minute checkpoint at week 3 with SEs, eng leads, and a runbook of what we changed.
[07:49] Jordan: yes week 3 mid-point is locked. final readout — we'll aim for an exec-friendly 30 minute deck on week 6. who will attend from your side?
[07:59] Ravi: CTO + Head of Product + Procurement — so we need cost clarity and risk notes in the deck.
[08:07] Jordan: we'll prepare a cost appendix with hosted vs dedicated numbers and an ops risk slide (VPC/KMS timeline, dependency on custom prompts).
[08:15] Carlos: pricing model question — how do you account for caching lowering token count? if our cache avoids re-sending context, do you charge on actual emitted tokens?
[08:25] Jordan: we bill on tokens processed; caching can reduce input token volume by deduping common prefixes, but some dedup strategies (KV caching) are internal optimizations and could change cost dynamics. We'll show modeled numbers and note assumptions.
[08:40] Mei: any objections on data residency? we need EU-only region for some datasets.
[08:47] Priya: we can run the POC in eu-west region for the relevant datasets; for dedicated you'd be able to pin region. hosted default might route to closest region but we can explicit region pin for runs.
[08:58] Asha: tokenization — last time we saw a mismatch because of emoji and non-latin characters. i'd like to flag this for the runner.
[09:06] Priya: noted, we'll include unicode-heavy samples in the test set.
[09:12] 
[09:30] Jordan: recap — milestone plan: Kickoff/Access (this week) -> Small runs + tuning (week1-2) -> Mid-point review (wk3) -> Dedicated tests & optimizations (wk4-5) -> Exec readout (wk6). action owners as assigned.
[09:49] Carlos: that works. can you share a sample POC contract or SOW? procurement will want a one-pager.
[09:56] Jordan: yes i'll attach a templated SOW and an optional Dedicated pricing sheet.
[10:03] Ravi: any blockers you foresee from your side?
[10:07] Priya: main blocker is access; if VPC/KMS approvals slip it could push the mid-point review. Also if sample traces are delayed we'll have to infer traffic shape from heuristics which reduces confidence.
[10:20] Asha: we'll triage access first and get SSO/SAML metadata to you by Friday.
[10:25] Mei: we'll export 24h of traffic and a golden prompt set and send by Monday.
[10:29] Jordan: great. last quick Q — do you want us to run a comparative run against Anthropic as a baseline? sometimes customers request third-party baselines.
[10:40] Carlos: yes include Anthropic as a competitor baseline if it's low lift. procurement likes apples-to-apples.
[10:47] Priya: we can do a standardized baseline but it'll add a day to runs. is that ok?
[10:52] Carlos: fine.
[11:00] Jordan: awesome. Evan will circulate the milestone calendar + checklist by Friday. Priya will send the benchmark spreadsheet and runner instructions. Mei & Asha to provide artifacts. any final questions?
[11:12] Ravi: none from product. thanks everyone.
[11:16] Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up in email with dates.

End of transcript.
